description: Curated official-source registry for the Reg Mitra regulatory retrieval corpus. | GST 2.0 rate notifications (Notification 9/2025-CT(R) etc.) pend on host taxinformation.cbic.gov.in which is unreachable from the build network — see docs.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Power to condone delay in filing Form No. 10A under section 12A(1)(ac)(i)
sources.applicability: Trusts and institutions that filed Form 10A late and have a condonation application pending or filed on or after the circular date.
sources.seedText: CBDT clarifies that the jurisdictional Principal Commissioner or Commissioner of Income-tax has power to condone delay in filing Form 10A under section 12A(1)(ac)(i). The circular applies where Form 10A was filed late and the condonation application is pending or is filed on or after the circular date.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Extension for issuing TDS certificates for the quarter ended 31 December 2025
sources.applicability: Deductors issuing TDS certificates under section 203 read with rule 31 for the quarter ended 31 December 2025.
sources.seedText: For the quarter ended 31 December 2025, CBDT extended the due date for issuing TDS certificates under section 203 read with rule 31 to 31 March 2026 because of e-filing portal technical glitches. This was a one-time extension and is now historical.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Forms for notification and quarterly reporting by Sovereign Wealth Funds
sources.applicability: Sovereign wealth funds seeking or holding notification under Schedule V of the Income-tax Act, 2025.
sources.seedText: CBDT specifies Form I for a sovereign wealth fund seeking notification and Form II for quarterly reporting of investments. An already-notified fund does not file a fresh Form I but must file Form II within one month after each quarter. The circular is effective from 1 April 2026 for tax year 2026-27 and later years.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Condonation of delay in electronically filing Form No. 10AB for approval under section 80G(5)
sources.applicability: Applicants seeking approval under clause (ii) of the first proviso to section 80G(5) whose Form 10AB was filed late.
sources.seedText: Official CBDT publication concerning condonation of delay in electronically filing Form 10AB for approval under clause (ii) of the first proviso to section 80G(5). The source page identifies it as Circular No. 6/2026 dated 2 July 2026. The circular text must be checked before advising on eligibility or procedure.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: CBDT circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for CBDT circulars; not sufficient by itself for a legal conclusion.
sources.seedText: Official CBDT circulars index used to discover new publications and verify that a retrieved circular remains current. Open the underlying circular before relying on a substantive conclusion.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN
sources.applicability: CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
sources.seedText: CBIC clarifies that a communication generated through the GST common portal under section 169 and bearing a verifiable RFN does not also require a DIN. The RFN-bearing communication is valid. Circulars 122/41/2019-GST and 128/47/2019-GST stand modified to that extent.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: Review, revision and appeal for orders passed by Common Adjudicating Authorities
sources.applicability: Orders-in-Original passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority for show-cause notices issued by DGGI.
sources.seedText: For orders passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority, the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner under whom that authority is posted is the reviewing authority under section 107 and the revisional authority under section 108. Appeals lie to the Commissioner (Appeals) corresponding to that territorial jurisdiction.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: CBIC central GST circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for central GST circulars; not sufficient by itself for a legal conclusion.
sources.seedText: Official CBIC index for central GST circulars. Use it to discover newer circulars and to check number, date and subject, then open the underlying circular before relying on a conclusion.

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
sources.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
sources.seedText: Official GST portal user manual for preparing, saving, previewing and filing Form GSTR-1. Portal instructions support the mechanics of filing but do not by themselves determine legal applicability or a tax position.

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: GST welcome kit and GSTR-3B filing guidance
sources.applicability: Registered persons using the GST portal for return preparation and payment.
sources.seedText: Official GSTN guidance for new taxpayers covering core portal workflows, return preparation and payment. Treat portal guidance as procedural support and verify current due dates or legal positions against the current notification or circular.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: Tax payment and TDS payment frequently asked questions
sources.applicability: Taxpayers and deductors using the Income Tax e-filing portal for tax payments.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal help for tax payments. Use it for current portal mechanics and payment troubleshooting, while checking the Act, Rules and applicable CBDT publication for the underlying obligation and deadline.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: ITR-1 online filing and advance-tax guidance
sources.applicability: Individuals evaluating ITR-1 eligibility or using the e-filing portal, subject to statutory eligibility conditions.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing guidance on ITR-1 filing and related payment steps. Confirm form eligibility and the substantive tax position against the current Act, Rules, instructions and notifications.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: Deferment of the mandatory effective date of SQM 1 and SQM 2
sources.applicability: Firms performing audits, reviews, assurance or related-services engagements under ICAI standards.
sources.seedText: ICAI deferred the mandatory effective date of SQM 1 and SQM 2, which had been scheduled for 1 April 2026, until a further announcement. SQC 1 continues to remain in force and applicable in the meantime. The announcement was issued under the authority of the ICAI Council.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: Guidance Note on Audit of Banks — 2026 edition
sources.applicability: Members conducting statutory audits of banks for the relevant audit cycle.
sources.seedText: Official ICAI landing page for the 2026 edition of the Guidance Note on Audit of Banks. Use the linked complete guidance note and the engagement's applicable RBI directions and auditing standards before reaching an audit conclusion.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: ICAI Accounting Standards index
sources.applicability: Discovery of ICAI Accounting Standards; applicability depends on the reporting framework, entity and period.
sources.seedText: Official ICAI Accounting Standards index. Retrieve the full current standard and check the entity's reporting framework and period before applying a recognition, measurement, presentation or disclosure conclusion.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: ICAI Auditing and Assurance Standards Board resources
sources.applicability: Discovery of engagement and quality-control standards, guidance notes and AASB announcements.
sources.seedText: Official ICAI Auditing and Assurance Standards Board resource page. Use it to locate the complete applicable standard, guidance note and current announcement for the engagement.

sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
sources.title: SEBI circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for active SEBI circulars across regulated intermediaries.
sources.seedText: Official SEBI active-circular index. At the latest recorded check it contained current 2026 circulars. Use it to discover later publications and open the underlying circular before relying on any compliance conclusion.

sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
sources.title: SEBI master circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery of consolidated SEBI master circulars; confirm subsequent amendments from the active circular index.
sources.seedText: Official SEBI master-circular index. A master circular consolidates material to its stated cut-off date; later circulars can amend it, so check the active circular index as well.

sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
sources.title: Special window for transfer and dematerialisation of physical securities
sources.applicability: Holders, listed entities, RTAs and intermediaries dealing with eligible physical-securities transfer cases described in the circular.
sources.seedText: Official SEBI circular dated 30 January 2026 concerning a special window for specified physical-securities transfer and dematerialisation cases. Read the complete circular to confirm eligibility, window dates, documentary conditions and intermediary responsibilities.

sources.publisher: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation
sources.title: EPFO employer and contribution frequently asked questions
sources.applicability: Establishments and employers covered by the EPF & MP Act and schemes.
sources.seedText: Official EPFO frequently asked questions. The employer must electronically file wage-month information through ECR and, under paragraph 38(1), pay contributions within fifteen days after the close of the month. Verify any temporary relief, extension or portal change against a current EPFO publication.

sources.publisher: Reserve Bank of India
sources.title: Qualifying Assets Criteria for Non-Banking Financial Company — Micro Finance Institutions
sources.applicability: Non-Banking Financial Company — Micro Finance Institutions and their qualifying-assets classification under the applicable RBI regulatory framework.
sources.seedText: RBI/2025-26/44 dated 6 June 2025 prescribes that an NBFC-MFI must maintain qualifying assets constituting at least sixty per cent of its total assets, net of intangible assets, on an ongoing basis. The circular states that the instructions take immediate effect. Read the complete RBI publication and applicable Master Direction before concluding on classification.

sources.publisher: Reserve Bank of India
sources.title: Compliance Function and Role of Chief Compliance Officer in NBFCs
sources.applicability: Upper Layer and Middle Layer NBFCs within the scope and implementation timetable stated in the RBI circular.
sources.seedText: Official RBI circular on an independent compliance function and the role of the Chief Compliance Officer in specified NBFCs. Applicability and implementation timing differ by NBFC layer. Use the complete circular to verify board responsibilities, appointment criteria, tenure, reporting line and review requirements.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
sources.title: The Companies Act, 2013
sources.applicability: Companies and other persons or matters within the provisions of the Companies Act, subject to commencement notifications, later amendments, rules and exemptions.
sources.seedText: Official MCA text of the Companies Act, 2013. A conclusion must also account for the relevant provision's commencement, later amending Acts, applicable rules, exemptions, notifications and MCA circulars; the base Act alone is not a complete statement of every current company-law obligation.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: FSSAI Advisories and Orders index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for FSSAI advisories and orders; the underlying publication controls.
sources.seedText: Official FSSAI Advisories and Orders index. Use it to find later publications and open the complete underlying advisory or order before relying on a compliance conclusion.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: FSSAI Gazette Notifications index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for FSSAI regulations and amendment notifications; the gazetted instrument controls.
sources.seedText: Official FSSAI Gazette Notifications index. Use it to identify the complete gazetted regulation, its commencement clause and subsequent amendments before applying a legal requirement.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: Enforcement against prohibited use of calcium carbide and unsafe ethylene in artificial ripening of fruits
sources.applicability: Food business operators, fruit traders, ripening facilities and enforcement officials involved in artificial ripening of fruits.
sources.seedText: FSSAI's advisory dated 16 April 2026 reiterates that calcium carbide is prohibited for artificial ripening under Regulation 2.3.5 and that direct contact of fruits with ethylene in powder or liquid form is prohibited. It directs inspection and enforcement activity. Read the full advisory for the prescribed handling, chamber and enforcement guidance.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Amendment Regulations, 2026
sources.applicability: Food business operators, petty food businesses, street food vendors and licensing authorities within the amended regulations.
sources.seedText: The 2026 amendment revises licensing and registration requirements, including treatment of specified street food vendors, continuity of licences and registrations unless suspended, cancelled or surrendered, consequences tied to annual fees or returns, a thirty-day closure-intimation requirement and risk-based inspection or audit provisions. Apply the exact amended text and transition provisions to the food business concerned.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026
sources.applicability: Food business operators subject to the amended production, raw-material and storage-record requirements, with stated exceptions.
sources.seedText: The FSSAI Second Amendment Regulations, 2026 introduce record requirements for manufacturing food business operators and storage controls including first-in-first-out or first-expiry-first-out principles, subject to the text's scope and exceptions. Confirm the gazette date and exact commencement clause from the complete notification before setting a compliance deadline.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (full text as enacted)
sources.applicability: All persons registered or liable to be registered under GST; governs levy, input tax credit, returns, late fee, interest, demands and service of notice under central GST law.
sources.seedText: Official CBIC page carrying the complete English text of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, including the chapters on levy and collection, input tax credit (section 16 conditions for availing ITC), returns, demands and recovery, and service of notice. Section 47 (Levy of late fee) prescribes one hundred rupees for each day a return under section 39 or 45 remains unfiled, subject to a cap. Section 50 (Interest on delayed payment of tax) provides for interest at a rate not exceeding eighteen per cent as notified. Sections 73 and 74 govern determination of tax not paid, short paid or erroneously refunded, and input tax credit wrongly availed, without and with fraud or wilful misstatement respectively, including show-cause notice procedure. Section 169 specifies the permitted modes of service of notice, order or other communication. Note: this page carries the Act as enacted in 2017; later amendments (for example section 74A inserted for FY 2024-25 onwards) are not reflected and must be checked against current amending Acts and notifications.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.applicability: Registered persons and GST officers; prescribes the procedural rules for registration, invoicing, input tax credit, returns and payment under the CGST Act.
sources.seedText: Official CBIC PDF of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Rules, 2017, notified vide Notification No. 3/2017-Central Tax dated 19 June 2017 and stated on its face to be as amended by Notifications No. 7/2017, 10/2017 and 15/2017-Central Tax. It contains the procedural framework for registration, tax invoices, input tax credit, returns and payment of tax under the CGST Act. Note: this document reflects the Rules as they stood at 1 July 2017; the Rules have been amended many times since, so the current amended rule text must be confirmed from a later CBIC notification before relying on a specific procedural requirement.
sources.title: Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Rules, 2017 (as notified 19 June 2017)

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: FAQs on Form GSTR-3B (filing, due dates, nil return, late fee and interest)
sources.applicability: Normal and casual registered taxpayers required to file Form GSTR-3B monthly or quarterly, including those under the QRMP scheme.
sources.seedText: Official GST portal FAQ on Form GSTR-3B. It states that the due date for filing Form GSTR-3B for monthly filers is the 20th day of the month following the month (tax period) to which the return pertains, while for quarterly (QRMP) filers the due date, as notified for different States and UTs, is the 22nd or 24th day of the month following the quarter; the Government may extend the due date by notification. Form GSTR-3B must be filed even if there is no business in the period, and can be filed as a Nil return where there are no transactions and no liability, including late fee, interest or ITC, to report. The FAQ also covers payment of late fee (including carried-forward late fee of the previous tax period), system-computed interest, and Nil filing through the online mode and SMS.

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: Manual — creating, saving, paying taxes and filing Form GSTR-3B
sources.applicability: Normal registered taxpayers declaring and discharging GST liabilities for a tax period in Form GSTR-3B on the GST portal.
sources.seedText: Official GST portal user manual describing step by step how a taxpayer creates, saves, pays taxes and files Form GSTR-3B. Taxpayers are required to declare their GST liabilities for a tax period and discharge those liabilities in Form GSTR-3B, and a normal taxpayer must file the return for every applicable tax period even if there is no business activity. The manual walks through the return dashboard, auto-population from GSTR-1 and GSTR-2B, tile-wise entry of outward supplies and input tax credit, payment of tax through the electronic cash and credit ledgers, challan creation, and filing with DSC or EVC.

sources.publisher: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation, Ministry of Labour and Employment
sources.title: Present Rates of Contribution (EPF, EPS, EDLI and administrative/inspection charges)
sources.applicability: All establishments covered under the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and their employees; governs monthly statutory payroll deductions and employer liability.
sources.seedText: PRESENT RATES OF CONTRIBUTION. Employee EPF share: 12% (or 10% in specified cases); employee EPS/EDLI: nil. Employer: EPF equals the difference of the employee share and the pension contribution; EPS (A/C 10) 8.33%; EDLI (A/C 21) 0.50%. EPF administrative charges (A/C 2) are 0.50% w.e.f. 01-06-2018, minimum Rs.500 per month per establishment (Rs.75 if there is no contributory member); EDLI administrative charges are nil w.e.f. 01-04-2017. The 10% rate applies to establishments employing fewer than 20 persons, sick industrial companies declared by BIFR, establishments whose accumulated losses equal or exceed their entire net worth, and Jute, Beedi, Brick, Coir and Guar gum factories. Contributions are payable on a maximum wage ceiling of Rs.15,000; contribution on higher wages requires a joint request under Para 26(6) of the EPF Scheme, and the Rs.15,000 ceiling does not apply to International Workers. EPS contribution (8.33%) is paid out of the employer's share and is not payable after the employee crosses 58 years. EDLI contribution is capped at the Rs.15,000 ceiling even if PF is paid on higher wages. Establishments exempted under the PF Scheme pay inspection charges at 0.18% (minimum Rs.5); those exempted under EDLI pay 0.005% (minimum Re.1).

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: TDS Rates chart — Assessment Year 2026-27
sources.applicability: Deductors computing tax deductible at source on payments to residents and non-residents for Assessment Year 2026-27.
sources.seedText: Official Income Tax Department TDS Rates chart page under Tax Charts & Tables, presenting the rates for tax deduction at source for Assessment Year 2026-27, separately for persons other than companies and for companies, with rates to be increased by applicable surcharge and health and education cess where relevant. The chart is organised section-wise across the 192/193/194-series and 195, including salary (192), interest (194A), winnings (194B/194BB), contractor payments (194C), insurance commission (194D), professional and technical fees (194J), rent (194-I), immovable property transfers (194-IA), rent by certain individuals (194-IB), e-commerce (194-O) and purchase of goods (194Q). Read the exact rate and threshold for the specific section and payee status from the chart before computing a deduction.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Interest and Fees under the Income-tax Act (sections 234A, 234B, 234C, 234F and TDS/TCS defaults)
sources.applicability: Taxpayers and deductors liable to interest or fees for delayed filing, non-payment or short payment of advance tax, or TDS/TCS defaults.
sources.seedText: Official Income Tax Department tutorial on interest and fees, described as compensatory charges levied automatically without prior notice. Section 234A: 1% per month or part thereof on unpaid tax for delay in filing the return, from the due date to the actual filing date (or to completion of assessment where no return is filed). Section 234B: 1% per month on unpaid tax from 1 April to the date of regular assessment where advance tax paid is less than 90% of the assessed tax. Section 234C: 1% per month for underpayment of the advance-tax instalments benchmarked at 15%, 45%, 75% and 100%. Section 234F fee for late furnishing of the ITR: Rs.1,000 where total income does not exceed Rs.5,00,000 and Rs.5,000 otherwise, with no fee where the assessee is not liable to furnish a return; a fee under section 234-I applies to certain revised returns on the same slabs. For TDS/TCS defaults, section 201/206C interest runs at 1% per month for failure to deduct or collect and 1.5% per month for failure to deposit after deduction or collection. The page also notes situations where interest relief applies, including disputed demands under appeal and income earned abroad that foreign law restricts from remittance.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: FAQs on Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)
sources.applicability: Deductors and payees seeking official answers on the TDS mechanism, deduction obligations, credit for tax deducted and related compliance.
sources.seedText: Official Income Tax Department FAQ document on Tax Deducted at Source. It explains that for quick and efficient collection of taxes the Income-tax Law incorporates a system of deduction of tax at the point of generation of income, called Tax Deducted at Source, under which the payer deducts tax before making specified payments and deposits it with the Government, with the payee claiming credit for the deducted amount. The FAQs cover the deductor's obligations, the payments covered by the TDS mechanism, and how the payee's credit is reflected. Read the current section-wise rates from the TDS rate chart rather than this FAQ before computing a specific deduction.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: e-Proceedings FAQ — responding electronically to notices, intimations and letters
sources.applicability: Registered e-filing users and their authorised representatives responding to notices, intimations or letters issued by the Income Tax Department.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal FAQ on the e-Proceedings service, the electronic platform for conducting proceedings end to end on the e-filing portal. Any registered user or their authorised representative can view and submit a response to any notice, intimation or letter issued by the Income Tax Department. The FAQ describes the benefits of responding electronically — no need to visit the Income Tax Office, easier tracking of submissions and record keeping — the navigation path (log in, then Pending Actions > e-Proceedings), and clarifies mechanics of submitting responses, including that a submitted response does not require separate e-verification.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: e-Proceedings user manual — viewing and responding to income-tax notices
sources.applicability: Taxpayers responding through the e-filing portal to defective-return notices, prima facie adjustments, rectification and notices from the Assessing Officer or CPC.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal user manual for the e-Proceedings service, covering notices, intimations and letters issued by the Assessing Officer, CPC or any other Income Tax Authority. It lists the categories that can be viewed and responded to, including defective notice under section 139(9), prima facie adjustment under section 143(1)(a), suo-moto rectification under section 154, notices issued by the Assessing Officer or other authority, and information-seeking notices under sections 133(6) and 131 (including those addressed to another PAN/TAN). The manual gives the step-by-step screens for viewing a notice, submitting a response with attachments, and tracking the proceeding status.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: Reassessment proceedings FAQs — income escaping assessment (section 148, 1961 Act; sections 280-281, 2025 Act)
sources.applicability: Taxpayers who receive reassessment notices where income has escaped assessment, under section 148 of the 1961 Act or the corresponding provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal FAQ on reassessment proceedings. It maps the reassessment framework across the transition from section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 to the new Income-tax Act, 2025, describing the procedure for issuing a notice under section 280 of the 2025 Act where income has escaped assessment for the relevant tax year, including the preliminary information-and-opportunity procedure under section 281. It also explains the circumstances in which the Assessing Officer is not required to follow the section 281 procedure before issuing a section 280 notice, noting that even in such cases approval of the Additional Commissioner or Joint Commissioner is required. Useful for determining which regime and procedural safeguards apply to a reassessment notice received by a client.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: Response to Outstanding Demand — e-filing help and FAQs
sources.applicability: Taxpayers with an outstanding tax demand against their PAN who must pay or contest it through the e-filing portal.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing help page on responding to an outstanding demand. Where the Department finds an outstanding tax demand against a PAN, the taxpayer is given an opportunity to respond; if no response is submitted, the demand is confirmed and adjusted against any refund due or shown as demand payable. Demands are checked by logging in and navigating to Pending Actions > Response to Outstanding Demand, where each demand shows a status of pending payment or response with Pay Now and Submit Response options, and the taxpayer is also alerted by email and SMS. A taxpayer who disagrees in full or in part selects Disagree with demand, chooses from the listed reasons and provides supporting details for each, and is expected to pay the undisputed portion where the disagreement is partial.
